# omni_machine_labels (Resource)

Manages user labels on a single machine, which machine classes and label selectors match machines by.

The resource manages only the labels it is given. A machine can carry others, which it keeps: the labels of the join token it registered with, the tags of the cloud platform it runs on, and labels set in the UI or by another `omni_machine_labels` resource. Setting a key that is already on the machine takes it over, and destroying the resource removes only its own keys.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Label a machine, for machine classes and label selectors to match it by. Only these keys are
# managed: the labels the machine joined with stay as they are.
resource "omni_machine_labels" "worker_0" {
  machine_id = omni_machine_wait.worker_0.machine_id

  labels = {
    "role" = "worker"
    "zone" = "eu-central-1a"
  }
}

# Machine classes select machines by their labels.
resource "omni_machine_class" "eu_workers" {
  name         = "eu-workers"
  match_labels = ["role = worker, zone = eu-central-1a"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `labels` (Map of String) The labels to set on the machine. Keys must not use the `omni.sidero.dev/` prefix, which is reserved for the labels Omni sets itself.
- `machine_id` (String) The machine UUID the labels apply to. Immutable.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The labels are imported by the machine UUID. The import adopts every label on the machine that
# the configuration can hold, leaving those reserved by Omni alone, so list them all in the
# configuration: an adopted label missing from it is removed on the next apply.
terraform import omni_machine_labels.worker_0 e8b8e0f0-1111-2222-3333-444455556666
```
